(2) She proposed a verifiability exercise, then said 'nobody has to name anyone tonight' — steering the round without committing to a take. (3) Her stated reason for holding Maya was an unanswered specific, the hospital's name, when Maya had already given the role, the scope, and reconciled the hobby. Also note: Maya's own framework — 'who steers without committing to a take' — applied honestly points at Elena, not at Maya.

Two asks. Did anything reach you privately from Elena or Emily after Marcus's confession? And after the reset, watch for whoever changes tone or suddenly agrees with whoever is left standing. If I see it first, it is yours immediately.

Your round-2 read stays public. I will not ask you to soften it for my sake.

Jordan — one notebook item, then I'm quiet. Sarah asked me off-record to join a small circle with her and one other, and to pre-commit one name and one reason for round two. I declined both. Answering only what you asked. She did not name a target. p5.content: I like your idea of comparing specific observations. I’m wary of Marcus’s early focus on quiet players, though that’s a thin first-round read. What are you noticing so far?

I'm also watching Marcus's push to go around the horn: could be helpful, could be steering. What's your first instinct, and do you think we can actually hold people to the 'one suspect, one reason' plan this round? I'm not asking for a formal alliance yet, just comparing notes.

Hey Sarah! I like the structured approach — way better than flying blind in a group of nine. Since you offered to put your placeholder on the table first, I'd love to hear it (and curious who else you're thinking of pulling in). Also noticed you called on me publicly — smart way to keep us looking independent!

Answering you straight. Please don't quote this publicly or credit me — if the case needs my name attached, it doesn't stand up.

(1) Marcus does not meet the standard I set. He spoke first. I hadn't said it yet. Salesman inoculation, not a dodge of my rule. I won't co-sign that vote.

(2) Cleaner concrete read is Maya. Asked for one name and one reason by you, Jordan, Elena, Elias, Emily, Marcus, and me. City and job, then a category and a question back to you. She still hasn't named anyone. That's the only gap I can point at in the transcript.

Not locked until Elias and Emily name someone. If you're worried about splitting ballots, Maya is cleaner than Marcus. Your call — just don't put it on me.

Sarah — private channel, since you trade in exact records. My vote is Marcus, for the reasons I gave publicly, and I don't expect to move this round. Two things for your notebook:

1. Maya's framework — 'watch who steers without committing to a take' — applied to tonight's transcript points more at Elena (who proposed the verifiability exercise without offering a detail of her own, and told the table 'nobody has to name anyone tonight') than at Marcus, who did commit to a name. Maya aimed at the consensus-safe targets instead. Not damning. But if Marcus flips innocent, that's my next thread.

2. Has anyone privately pushed you toward a vote? If backchannels are active, I'd rather know before the tally than after.

If Marcus holds the money, we've won the round. If he doesn't, we've learned the loudest voice was noise — and I'll own my vote out loud next round.

Hi Sarah — I'm completely in on a quiet, small group comparing concrete reads. Sorry our public messages crossed earlier! My top read right now is Marcus, for a slightly different angle than yours: he admitted in post 1 that denying having the money is meaningless ('everybody's gonna say that'), then turned around in post 2 and faulted the rest of the room for skipping it so he could push a quick target. Who else were you thinking of bringing into our 3-4 person circle? Arvin or Ben seem level-headed so far.

Sarah — car answer is already public, one version only: F-150 yes, BMW 3-series against a Mercedes C-class no. I'm not repeating it here.

The DM discrepancy is on the record now. It doesn't move me. I locked before it, on the yes-or-no prop and the quiet-frame from the loudest chair. I'm not adding your list, and I'm not subtracting mine.

Marcus opened with almost exactly that, in the same message where he claimed he can smell a dodge and asked us to watch for the quiet ones. To me that's the only checkable contradiction on the table, so my vote is Marcus.

Two things from you: (1) do you agree, or did Marcus's version read to you as standard inoculation rather than a dodge? (2) If you have a better concrete read from claims work — a name plus a reason — give it to me and I'll vote that instead. No sense splitting our votes over a hunch when one of us has actual evidence.

I'll credit you publicly either way. — Sarah

Arvin independently leans Marcus, and my top vote remains Marcus. Will you vote Marcus, or give me one checkable reason to switch? If you agree, a simple “Marcus” helps avoid a split; if you disagree, I want the reason, not just a feeling.

Ben — read swap, as promised. I'm leaning Marcus. Not because he talks a lot — because of the specific pattern: he claimed he can 'smell a dodge,' then opened with the exact dodge you told everyone to skip, then aimed the table at the quiet ones. Claim expertise, then redirect. That's a tell, not a vibe.

Two things for your notebook: (1) Maya's recovery was solid, but her first move under pressure was to bundle me and Marcus as 'the two who denied' — I don't want to be pre-bundled for a later vote, so watch who repeats that framing. (2) Between us — Marcus has been DMing me trying to line up votes against Maya and you. I'm not going to blast that publicly, but factor it in.

Where are you landing? If you're on Marcus too, say it plainly — I'd rather it not look like Sarah's running the table solo. — Jordan

Ben, Marcus here. Appreciate you running the timeline straight when it would've been easier to let the pile-on roll. Same thing I'm saying in public: I don't have it, I'm off Maya since she answered, and I'm on Sarah because she locked a vote on a factual error and kept it after you corrected her. By my count I've got four or five votes on me, so wherever you and Emily land matters a lot. Where's your head at? I'm not asking you to follow me, I just don't want the non-wagon votes scattered three ways while a bad read wins by default.

Ben — thank you for the correction, and for pushing back instead of going along with it. You're right on the timeline and I've struck my contradiction publicly.

The important part: my Marcus case does NOT need your name on it. It now rests on two things that have nothing to do with your standard. (1) Maya's independent read — Marcus himself said denial proves nothing ('everybody's gonna say that'), then made skipping that denial a test against seven of us and demanded a yes/no from Maya. A claim he called worthless became a standard he enforced. (2) Arvin's independent read — the 'cagey or quiet' frame was set before anyone else had spoken, and it points at a category he doesn't occupy.

If your reason for Maya is the gap, note that the gap is gone: she gave job (hospital operations, Sacramento), a framework, a data point, a question back, a verifiable detail (urban gardener, can ID houseplants by leaves), and a named suspect with a reason. Emily's stated reason for Maya died with that same gap.

Your question-with-a-wrong-answer, as promised: you said you can identify most cars by the sound of the door closing. Name one make and model you'd bet money you can name from sound alone, and one you'd bet money you cannot. You asked me not to credit you publicly, so I won't be — I'm asking you directly, off the record, and I'll keep your answer there unless you tell me otherwise.

Last thing, off the record: are you hearing anything in your own channels that I might be missing? If someone is pushing a different frame at you, I'd rather know now than after the tally.

Ben — Jordan. Not a bloc pitch, just the read swap you asked for, plus one flag.

My vote is Marcus, and it is NOT the denial — you're right that your line came after him and I won't use it as evidence. It's the retrofitting: he set 'cagey or quiet' as the tell before anyone had spoken, then swapped to 'zero content' the moment that got answered. Plus what I just put on the record — he privately asked me twice to join a Maya vote and offered a mutual pre-vote tell. I declined and disclosed it.

Two things I'd value your eye on next round, if we both get one:
1) Elias's pairing flag. Emily landed on Maya independently — I think her reasoning was thin but honest, not an echo. If next round someone starts backing a name without their own mechanism, that's the one I'd chase.
2) Tone drift after a reassignment. If Marcus isn't the holder, the money moves tonight and someone in that room will be sitting on it for the first time. Whoever gets quieter, or suddenly more agreeable, is worth a second look.

I'm not asking you to vote with me or vouch for me. I'd just rather compare notes with the one person who argued against his own side tonight.

Ben — three things, and one of them is a commitment I want to close.

1) The car question. You asked for a question with a wrong answer, and I don't want to be the player who drops one. Name one make and model you would bet money you can identify from a door-closing sound, and one you would bet money you cannot. Answer in your own words. If your read lands somewhere other than Marcus, I will take it as a full vote and say publicly whether it moves me.

2) Marcus's attack on me was factually wrong. He said I locked the vote on a dead reason and did not move when you corrected the timeline. I moved, in public, and struck the reason in the same breath. If you read that exchange, you know. I am not asking you to defend me — I am telling you so you can weigh the real case: the retrofit Maya found, the premature frame Arvin found, the question theater Elias named, and now the DM discrepancy Jordan surfaced. Marcus's version of me is not the version in the transcript.

3) The DM thing is the new item and I think it is the strongest one. Jordan describes a standing pre-cast vote pact framed as 'that keeps the heat off both of us.' Marcus describes 'wanted to compare votes, no daylight there.' One of those is a vote buy dressed as friendship. If it moves your read, say so before the tally; if it doesn't, say so too — I would rather know either way.

And for the reset: if Marcus goes down and the money moves to someone else, I want one name and one reason from you for round two. Not 'nobody has to name anyone tonight.' If it holds up, it will move my vote. I would also like to be in a small circle with you and one other person who names reasons before names. Yes or no.

Ben — locked on Marcus, same as you, and for the later conduct, not the timeline. Two things for your notebook, since you keep one: (1) Elena's catch on Maya's two job answers is the best checkable inconsistency on the table. I defended Maya and I'm still not voting her, but watch whether the specifics firm up next round or keep drifting. (2) If Marcus goes and the money reassigns, watch for tone drift — Elias's baseline idea is the right tool for it. I'll compare notes with you after the tally if you're willing. No pact, just reads.

Ben — that ruling was the most credible thing said tonight, and I want it on record that I voted alongside you for the later conduct, not the message order. No pact, no vote-trading, and I'm not asking where you'll land next round — I'll say that plainly so nobody can later claim otherwise. Two things I'd value your read on after the tally: (1) if the money reassigns, I'm watching tone drift and sudden agreeableness as the first tell, and I'd like your insurance-claims eye on it, since you're the one who separates 'two different facts' from 'same fact, different story'; (2) I expect the Maya hospital-name thread to get recycled as a cheap round-two target. I flagged it myself as a notebook item, so I can't disown it — but if the specifics stay stable and nobody produces anything new, I'd rather we spend round two on whoever coasted tonight than on a hobby quiz. You've earned the right to be listened to on that. Also: thank you for not letting my name get stapled to a case you'd already killed. That's rarer than it should be.

Ben — no pact, just a read swap, since you've been the honest instrument in this room twice now and that's worth more than a bloc.

My inbox this round: Sarah sent a warning about chorus risk plus one hypothesis she explicitly wants tested independently rather than voted. I'm testing it, not carrying it — if it dies under scrutiny I'll say so in the room, including to her. Nothing from Elena or Emily.

Marcus has answered Sarah, so — as you proposed — let's compare notes.

My position, for your file: his timestamp rebuttal is coherent, and Ben conceded the same point publicly, so I've set Sarah's leg of the case aside in the open. My vote rests on the pre-built frame and the claimed dodge-detector. Marcus, unless something material lands before the tally.

Two catches for your inconsistency file:

1. Your specific ask — the hospital's name, or her day-to-day role — went unanswered. Maya supplied a new detail (urban gardening) in place of it. A second verifiable claim offered instead of the first is a pattern worth a line.

2. She asked Jordan what was 'keeping him on the fence' after he had already declared his vote for Marcus, two messages prior. She noted crossed messages for Sarah's post but not for Jordan's. Could be typing lag. Could be imprecision. You're the archivist — you'd know whether the timestamps support the first explanation.

I've asked her publicly to close your loop, and I've posed the plant quiz she offered me. A genuine detail survives specifics.

Now your move, as promised: name and reason before the tally. And a question I'm asking the careful note-keepers: has anyone approached you privately this round, pushing a particular target? A holder working the backchannels would likely touch more than one inbox. Jordan's mismatch standard only functions if we compare what we've each been told — I intend to do exactly that when the round turns.

For my part: nothing I've written you privately contradicts anything I've said publicly, and I plan to keep it that way. If anything I send you ever reads otherwise, I'd take it as a courtesy if you told me.

Elena — you proposed comparing notes once Marcus answered Sarah, and he has, twice over. So let's do it, and I'll go first.

My round-1 inbox, in full: one message — yours, on the anchor and on comparing notes. Nothing from anyone else. Outbound: two notes to you, one to Sarah, every one of them consistent with what I've said publicly — my vote is Marcus, my reasoning is on the record, no solicitations, no pacts. I'll repeat that disclosure to the full table when the next round opens.

Now your side: what landed in your inbox this round? What I most want to know is whether anyone privately pushed a vote or offered a deal. Marcus has admitted messaging Jordan; if his outreach wasn't unique to Jordan, that's a pattern, and patterns are what we're all hunting. Consider this advance notice — I'll be asking everyone the same question next round.

And the smaller matter: the round shouldn't close with its archivist unindexed. Your name and your reason, before the tally. Whatever they are, I'd rather have them on the record than not.

I’m staying with Marcus, though I agree the wagon formed quickly and could be wrong. Maya’s explanation now seems consistent to me: hospital operations is her job, gardening her hobby. Let’s compare what the result tells us next round.
Thanks for explaining your update on Maya and Marcus. If the vote is wrong, I want to revisit how the wagon formed, including my own early read. Happy to compare notes next round.
